title: Dynegy Moss Landing Power Plant Hybrid: Moss Landing Vistra Battery Fire Response Timeline
summary: EPA's June 2026 update said 33,943 intact batteries from the burned area had been de-energized and were ready for recycling, with about 5,000 remaining in difficult or unsafe areas. Entity test: The later official record verifies corrective-action progress and an incident boundary while blocking a facility-wide availability or return-to-service claim.
key_findings: The timeline records supervised removal progress and no flareups during the December 2025 removal update while the cause of the January 2025 fire remained under investigation.
Alternative-explanation test: Tests incident and outage conditions, battery-unit differences, and operating-history alternatives.
Compatibility: The records concern the 300 MW fire-affected battery building inside the broader Moss Landing complex; they are not a common 750 MW plant-performance observation.
why_it_matters: This record either supplies a later compatible observation or tests a named Phase 56C alternative explanation without turning association into causal proof.
ftfn_relevance: Preserves the Phase 56C parent dossier and stable entity identifier.
Maps the record to named alternative explanations.
Separates observed result, attribution, independent validation, and unresolved denominators.
evidence_limits: The response applies to the 300 MW Moss Landing battery building and must not be silently assigned to every generator under the broader EIA plant identity.
Regulator-verified work status; root cause, complete removal, return to service, and plant-wide performance remain unresolved.
No causal effect, ranking, composite score, readiness score, or unsupported cross-entity comparison is supported.
